presences.label: Jerusalem
presences.note: First community of Jesus' followers after Pentecost, led by Peter, John and James.

presences.label: Damascus
presences.note: Disciples present when Paul was converted; Ananias baptised him.

presences.label: Antioch
presences.note: First mixed Jewish–Gentile church, where believers were called 'Christians'; base of Paul's missions.

presences.label: Rome
presences.note: Christians present by Claudius' expulsion of Jews (c. 49); Paul wrote to them c. 57.

presences.label: Philippi
presences.note: First church in Europe, founded by Paul with Lydia's household.

presences.label: Thessalonica
presences.note: Church founded by Paul; recipient of the earliest Christian letter.

presences.label: Corinth
presences.note: Paul stayed eighteen months; a lively, divided church addressed in 1–2 Corinthians.

presences.label: Ephesus
presences.note: Paul's base for nearly three years; later linked to John and Mary in tradition.

presences.label: Muziris (Kerala)
presences.note: Traditional landing of the apostle Thomas and origin of the St Thomas Christians.

presences.label: Alexandria
presences.note: Church traditionally founded by Mark; later a great see and centre of learning.

presences.label: Smyrna
presences.note: Church of Polycarp, addressed by Ignatius and Revelation.

presences.label: Lyon
presences.note: Greek-speaking church in Gaul; martyrs of 177; Irenaeus bishop.

presences.label: Carthage
presences.note: Heart of Latin-speaking North African Christianity (Scillitan martyrs, Tertullian, Cyprian).

presences.label: Edessa
presences.note: Centre of Syriac-speaking Christianity by c. 200; church building recorded in 201.

presences.label: Dura-Europos
presences.note: Oldest securely dated house church, with painted baptistery.

presences.label: Seleucia-Ctesiphon
presences.note: See of the catholicos of the Church of the East, organised by c. 280–410.

presences.label: Vagharshapat (Etchmiadzin)
presences.note: Mother cathedral of Armenia, first Christian kingdom (trad. 301).

presences.label: Tabennisi (Pachomian monasteries)
presences.note: Pachomius' communal monasteries in the Thebaid.

presences.label: Council of Nicaea
presences.note: First ecumenical council; Nicene Creed.

presences.label: Aksum
presences.note: Kingdom of Aksum adopts Christianity under Ezana, taught by Frumentius.

presences.label: Constantinople
presences.note: New Rome; seat of the Ecumenical Patriarch.

presences.label: Mtskheta (Georgia)
presences.note: Conversion of King Mirian of Kartli through Nino.

presences.label: Council of Constantinople
presences.note: Second ecumenical council; Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed.

presences.label: Merv
presences.note: Bishop of Merv attends the synod of 424; gateway of East Syriac mission to Central Asia.

presences.label: Council of Ephesus
presences.note: Third ecumenical council; Theotokos affirmed.

presences.label: Armagh (Ireland)
presences.note: Patrick's mission to Ireland (traditional date).

presences.label: Council of Chalcedon
presences.note: Fourth ecumenical council; definition of two natures; Oriental Orthodox separate.

presences.label: Nisibis
presences.note: Theological school of the Church of the East.

presences.label: Najran (Arabia)
presences.note: Christian city in southern Arabia; martyrs of c. 523.

presences.label: Faras (Nubia)
presences.note: Nubian kingdoms converted 543–580; Faras cathedral frescoes.

presences.label: Iona
presences.note: Columba's monastery, centre of Celtic mission.

presences.label: Canterbury
presences.note: Augustine's mission from Rome to the English.

presences.label: Chang'an (Xi'an)
presences.note: Alopen's Church of the East mission received by Emperor Taizong.

presences.label: Synod of Whitby
presences.note: Northumbria adopts Roman Easter reckoning.

presences.label: Baghdad
presences.note: Seat of Catholicos Timothy I, whose church stretched from Syria to China.

presences.label: Samarkand
presences.note: Metropolitan see of the Church of the East in Central Asia (8th century).

presences.label: Second Council of Nicaea
presences.note: Seventh ecumenical council restores icons.

presences.label: Kollam (Quilon)
presences.note: Tharisapalli copper plates grant privileges to Syrian Christians.

presences.label: Great Moravia
presences.note: Cyril and Methodius introduce Slavonic liturgy.

presences.label: Cluny
presences.note: Reforming Benedictine abbey.

presences.label: Mount Athos
presences.note: Great Lavra founded; Athos becomes heart of Orthodox monasticism.

presences.label: Gniezno (Poland)
presences.note: Baptism of Mieszko I.

presences.label: Kyiv
presences.note: Baptism of Rus' under Vladimir.

presences.label: Iceland
presences.note: Althing adopts Christianity.

presences.label: Kerait steppe
presences.note: Conversion of the Kerait to Church of the East Christianity.

presences.label: Lalibela
presences.note: Rock-hewn churches of the Zagwe kings.

presences.label: Fourth Lateran Council
presences.note: Transubstantiation defined; annual confession.

presences.label: Karakorum
presences.note: Church of the East clergy at the Mongol court; Rubruck's debate.

presences.label: Khanbaliq (Beijing)
presences.note: Franciscan John of Montecorvino's mission; East Syriac archdiocese.

presences.label: Trinity Lavra
presences.note: Sergius of Radonezh's monastery, heart of Russian monasticism.

presences.label: Council of Constance
presences.note: Ends the Western Schism; Hus burned.

presences.label: Council of Florence
presences.note: Short-lived reunion with Greeks, Armenians and Copts.

presences.label: Mbanza Kongo
presences.note: Kingdom of Kongo adopts Catholicism.

presences.label: Goa
presences.note: Portuguese capital in Asia; base for Xavier.

presences.label: Santo Domingo
presences.note: Montesinos' sermon against abuse of Indigenous people; first diocese in the Americas.

presences.label: Wittenberg
presences.note: Luther's Ninety-five Theses; Lutheran Reformation.

presences.label: Mexico City
presences.note: Twelve Franciscans begin the evangelisation of New Spain.

presences.label: Zürich
presences.note: Zwingli's Reformation; first Anabaptist baptisms.

presences.label: Lima
presences.note: Spanish foundation; archdiocese and centre of Andean Catholicism.

presences.label: Geneva
presences.note: Calvin's Reformed church and academy.

presences.label: Council of Trent
presences.note: Catholic response to the Reformation.

presences.label: Kagoshima
presences.note: Francis Xavier begins the Japan mission.

presences.label: Macau
presences.note: Portuguese settlement and gateway for missions to China and Japan.

presences.label: Cebu
presences.note: Permanent Spanish evangelisation of the Philippines begins.

presences.label: Nagasaki
presences.note: Port opened by Christian daimyō Ōmura Sumitada; centre of Japanese Christianity.

presences.label: Beijing
presences.note: Matteo Ricci admitted to the Ming capital.

presences.label: Jesuit reductions of Paraguay
presences.note: First Jesuit reduction among the Guaraní.

presences.label: Quebec
presences.note: Récollet and later Jesuit missions in New France.

presences.label: Synod of Dort
presences.note: Reformed synod against the Remonstrants.

presences.label: Massachusetts Bay
presences.note: Puritan Congregationalist colony.

presences.label: Westminster Assembly
presences.note: Westminster Confession and Catechisms.

presences.label: Mattancherry
presences.note: Coonan Cross Oath of the Thomas Christians.

presences.label: Tranquebar
presences.note: First Protestant mission in India.

presences.label: Godthåb (Nuuk), Greenland
presences.note: Hans Egede's Lutheran mission to the Inuit.

presences.label: Herrnhut
presences.note: Moravian revival and source of Moravian missions.

presences.label: St Thomas (Danish West Indies)
presences.note: Moravian mission to enslaved Africans.

presences.label: Northampton, Massachusetts
presences.note: Jonathan Edwards' revival; First Great Awakening.

presences.label: Genadendal (South Africa)
presences.note: Georg Schmidt's Moravian mission among the Khoikhoi.

presences.label: Seoul
presences.note: Korean scholars found a lay Catholic church.

presences.label: Sydney
presences.note: First Christian service in Australia.

presences.label: Freetown
presences.note: Black Christian settlers from Nova Scotia found Freetown.

presences.label: Tahiti
presences.note: London Missionary Society lands from the Duff.

presences.label: Serampore
presences.note: Carey, Marshman and Ward's mission and press.

presences.label: Cane Ridge
presences.note: Frontier camp-meeting revival.

presences.label: Guangzhou (Canton)
presences.note: Robert Morrison begins Protestant work in China.

presences.label: Bay of Islands (New Zealand)
presences.note: Marsden's Christmas Day sermon with Ruatara.

presences.label: Antananarivo
presences.note: LMS mission to Madagascar; later martyr church.

presences.label: Kailua-Kona (Hawai'i)
presences.note: American Board missionaries arrive.

presences.label: Samoa
presences.note: John Williams lands Tahitian teachers; Samoans adopt Christianity.

presences.label: Lakeba (Fiji)
presences.note: Wesleyan Methodist mission begins in Fiji.

presences.label: Badagry (near Lagos)
presences.note: Thomas Birch Freeman and CMS missionaries begin work in Yorubaland.

presences.label: Abeokuta
presences.note: Crowther's Yoruba mission; reunion with his mother.

presences.label: Onitsha
presences.note: Crowther's all-African Niger Mission.

presences.label: Hangzhou
presences.note: First base of the China Inland Mission.

presences.label: First Vatican Council
presences.note: Papal infallibility defined.

presences.label: Erub (Torres Strait)
presences.note: 'Coming of the Light': LMS Islander missionaries arrive, gateway to New Guinea.

presences.label: Buganda (Uganda)
presences.note: CMS missionaries reach Kabaka Mutesa's court; Catholics follow in 1879.

presences.label: Loughor (Wales)
presences.note: Welsh Revival under Evan Roberts.

presences.label: Mukti Mission, Kedgaon
presences.note: Revival at Pandita Ramabai's mission.

presences.label: Azusa Street, Los Angeles
presences.note: Pentecostal revival with global reach.

presences.label: Pyongyang
presences.note: Great Revival of Korean Protestantism.

presences.label: Valparaíso (Chile)
presences.note: Methodist Pentecostal revival under Willis Hoover.

presences.label: Edinburgh 1910
presences.note: World Missionary Conference.

presences.label: Belém (Brazil)
presences.note: Assemblies of God in Brazil founded by Daniel Berg and Gunnar Vingren.

presences.label: Dornakal
presences.note: V. S. Azariah becomes the first Indian Anglican bishop.

presences.label: Côte d'Ivoire coast
presences.note: William Wade Harris's mass movement.

presences.label: Nkamba (Congo)
presences.note: Simon Kimbangu's healing ministry.

presences.label: Ilesa (Nigeria)
presences.note: Aladura revival under Joseph Ayo Babalola.

presences.label: Barmen
presences.note: Confessing Church synod.

presences.label: Church of South India
presences.note: Union of Anglican, Methodist and Reformed churches.

presences.label: World Council of Churches
presences.note: Founding assembly of the WCC.

presences.label: Redeemed Christian Church of God, Lagos
presences.note: Founded by Josiah Akindayomi; later a global Nigerian Pentecostal network.

presences.label: Yoido Full Gospel Church, Seoul
presences.note: Founded 1958; became the world's largest congregation.

presences.label: Second Vatican Council
presences.note: Global Catholic council of renewal.

presences.label: Medellín
presences.note: Latin American bishops' conference; liberation theology.

presences.label: Lausanne Congress
presences.note: Global evangelical congress and Covenant.

presences.label: Toronto Airport Vineyard
presences.note: Toronto Blessing.

presences.label: Brownsville, Pensacola
presences.note: Brownsville Revival.

presences.label: Asbury University
presences.note: Asbury Revival.

presences.label: Jerusalem: Thomas to India (tradition)
presences.note: Traditional sea route of the apostle Thomas via the Red Sea trade to Muziris and Mylapore.

presences.label: Antioch: Paul's first journey
presences.note: Cyprus and southern Galatia with Barnabas (Acts 13–14).

presences.label: Antioch: Paul's second journey
presences.note: Into Europe: Philippi, Thessalonica, Athens and Corinth (Acts 15:36–18:22).

presences.label: Antioch: Paul's third journey
presences.note: Ephesus, Macedonia and Greece, then to Jerusalem (Acts 18:23–21:17).

presences.label: Caesarea: Paul's voyage to Rome
presences.note: Prisoner voyage via Crete and shipwreck on Malta (Acts 27–28).

presences.label: Tyre: Frumentius to Aksum
presences.note: Captive youths from Tyre reach the Aksumite court; Frumentius returns as bishop.

presences.label: Armagh: Celtic mission to Iona and Northumbria
presences.note: Columba to Iona (563); Aidan from Iona to Lindisfarne (635).

presences.label: Bangor: Columbanus to the continent
presences.note: Irish peregrinatio founding Luxeuil, Bregenz and Bobbio.

presences.label: Rome: Augustine to Canterbury
presences.note: Gregory the Great's mission to the English.

presences.label: Seleucia-Ctesiphon: Church of the East to China
presences.note: Silk Road route of East Syriac monks and merchants that brought Alopen to Chang'an.

presences.label: Constantinople: Cyril and Methodius to Moravia
presences.note: Mission to the Slavs and journey to Rome to defend Slavonic liturgy.

presences.label: Hamburg: Ansgar to Scandinavia
presences.note: Frankish mission to Hedeby and Birka.

presences.label: Constantinople: Franciscans to the Mongols
presences.note: William of Rubruck's journey to Möngke Khan at Karakorum (route approximate).

presences.label: Khanbaliq: Rabban Sauma to Europe
presences.note: Pilgrimage west and embassy to Constantinople, Rome, Paris and Gascony.

presences.label: Lisbon: Francis Xavier to Asia
presences.note: India, the Moluccas and Japan; died off the China coast.

presences.label: Macau: Jesuits to Beijing
presences.note: Ricci's step-by-step journey to the imperial capital.

presences.label: Herrnhut: Moravian missions
presences.note: Dober and Nitschmann sail via Copenhagen to St Thomas (1732).

presences.label: Dover: William Carey to Bengal
presences.note: Voyage round the Cape to Calcutta; settled at Serampore in 1800.

presences.label: London: Hudson Taylor's Lammermuir party
presences.note: China Inland Mission party sails to Shanghai and Hangzhou.

presences.label: Niger Delta: Crowther on the Niger
presences.note: The Dayspring expedition plants the Niger Mission at Onitsha and Lokoja.

presences.label: Los Angeles: Azusa missionaries to Asia
presences.note: A. G. and Lillian Garr carry the Pentecostal message to Calcutta and Hong Kong.

presences.label: Los Angeles: Pentecost to Europe and Africa
presences.note: T. B. Barratt brings Pentecostalism from New York to Oslo; Azusa missionaries reach Liberia.
